campaigns.title: Archive and Git merge behavior
campaigns.summary: Playbook item 7. The archive sweep and its two-file transaction, section archiving, the `tasks archive` surface, and the record-aware three-way merge git invokes as a merge driver. Sequenced after campaign 4 because every slice here either moves records the mutation slices wrote or merges two histories of them. Recurrence-aware selection stays with campaign 5 and the journal half of undo stays with campaign 6; both are named in the slices' oracle_gaps rather than assumed.

field_changes.title: Mutations: basic, placement, lifecycle, projects, delegation, and proposals
field_changes.summary: Playbook item 4 in full: create, changeset apply, update stamp, placement and delete on a real canonical writer, then the lifecycle half — state transitions and the DONE cascade, section and project mutation, delegation assignment and claim/release, proposal decisions, and the mutation `--json` envelopes. Seeded as one campaign because the playbook's item 4 is one item and campaign numbers are the playbook's; the second half was previously recorded only as a sentence saying it was not sliced, which `progress` could not count. Temporal verbs stay with campaign 5, revisions and the journal with campaign 6, archiving with campaign 7.

campaign_updates.reason: The record's summary asserted that lifecycle, proposals and delegation were 'the second half and are not sliced yet'. This proposal slices them, so that sentence becomes false on the day WIRING applies it. The title change follows the same fact.

slices.behavior: `tasks open`: selecting the link to act on, listing and refusing when a task has several, failing cleanly when it has none, launching through the TASKS_OPENER seam, and the `open --json` object naming the link opened
oracle_gaps: links-read deliberately excluded these five tests ('`open` is a separate command with a launcher seam'), and no slice picked them up; `lib/tasks/opener.rb` was in no slice's source_paths. This slice is that pickup, and it is also the `open --json` third of td-ee475f's mutation-envelope gap — the only one of the four envelope families named there that is a read.
The TUI's `o` binding shares Opener and is campaign 12; test/test_links_feature.rb's three TUI cases stay excluded exactly as links-read left them.

`Opener` shell-splits TASKS_OPENER and otherwise picks a platform launcher (`open`, `xdg-open`, `start`). Only the TASKS_OPENER path is tested, because that is how the suite observes an open without a browser. The platform default has no oracle at all on any platform, which is why this slice is platform-scoped rather than `any`.

Nothing asserts what `open` does when the resolved link is not a URL a launcher accepts, or when the launcher exits non-zero. Both are reachable from a real store and both need capture before translating.
slices.notes: The fixture wiring assumes porting/fixtures/valid/link-corpus lands under that name from the FIXTURES stream in this same push; it is the only fixture in the corpus with a task carrying several links, which is what the multi-link branch needs. If that directory is renamed, this becomes a fixtures_todo for exactly that shape. The launcher is an adapter seam in the port, not a syscall: a Go implementation that execs directly cannot be conformance-tested.

slices.behavior: The version gate on the read half of the CLI: every lenient read refuses a store declaring an unimplemented version, matching the strict paths and the API, while `check`, `config` and `help` still answer
oracle_gaps: Found by the SLICING survey, not by td-ee475f: test/test_schema_gate_reads.rb is a ten-test file in which NO test was claimed by any slice, and it is the CLI half of the rule six other slices' oracle_gaps call contract. The failure it exists to prevent is the worst read failure in the system and the least visible: a v3 store that renamed `title`/`state`/`tags` made `tasks list` print 'No matching tasks.' and `list --json` print `[]`, exit 0 — byte-identical to the answer for an empty store. An agent driving the CLI would conclude the user had nothing to do. A port that carries the store's gate but not the CLI's reproduces that bug exactly.

The gate is declared as data (`CliCommands::Command#gated?`, GATE_EXEMPT) with three exemptions, each carrying a written reason: `check` (it is the diagnostic the refusal sends you to), `config` (it reports where the store is, never what it contains) and `help` (it reads the registry). Porting the refusal without porting the exemptions produces a store nobody can diagnose — the refusal names `check`, and `check` would refuse too.

test/test_cli_json_coverage.rb#test_every_json_command_answers_in_json_when_it_refuses_an_unsupported_store and #test_gate_exempt_commands_still_answer_for_an_unsupported_store are the registry-wide statement of the same rule and are claimed by no slice: they run every entry in the RECIPES table, which includes verbs from campaigns 5, 6, 8 and 10. They belong to the final CLI-parity slice recorded in the SLICING survey.

The gate 'consults only the version header' — a store whose records are malformed but whose meta says 2 is NOT a version refusal, and is reported by the ordinary read path instead. Conflating the two is the expected defect and turns every parse error into a version error.

Schema-v1 migration and org-mode are out of scope (Marcus, 2026-08-01, no schema-v1 users exist) and td-09f7de removed them from Ruby, so this slice's oracle no longer carries them: there is no `tasks migrate`, no `migrate_schema!`, and no `migration_required` status. What remains IS contract and must be ported: any declared `meta` version other than 2 is refused identically, older or newer — `Check` reports `unsupported meta version <n> (expected 2)`, `Store#unsupported_schema?` gates mutations on both files, refusals carry the `:unsupported_schema` status and write nothing, and the API answers `503 unsupported_schema_version`. Omitting that gate is a data-corruption bug, not a skipped dead branch. Org-mode remains out of scope entirely.
slices.fixtures_todo: compat/future-schema-v3 declares version 3 but keeps v2 field names, so it proves the refusal without proving what the refusal PREVENTS. The case that matters is structurally different: a version-3 store whose records rename title/state/tags, which under a missing gate reads as an empty store rather than as an error. Also missing: a v1 store (declared version 1, v2-shaped records) and a v2 live file beside a v1 archive, which is the pair that proves the gate reads both files.
observable_outputs: stderr refusal text naming the version
stdout emptiness (nothing printed for a refused store)
slices.notes: Read this slice as the sibling of check-meta-and-ids: the same rule at the CLI boundary rather than at the checker. It is tiered high although it writes nothing, on the same reasoning as format-canonical-emit — the failure is silent, plausible, and destroys an agent's picture of the user's work.

slices.fixtures_todo: No fixture is a store whose records span the closed/open boundary in the shapes this slice turns on. Needed: (a) an open task carrying the `defer` tag, so the strip-on-close branch has a case (the corpus's `defer` gap is already recorded against four other slices); (b) a DONE task with an existing `closed` date older than today, which is the only input that distinguishes DONE→CANCELLED keeping the original stamp from re-stamping it; (c) a CANCELLED task, so reopening out of a non-DONE closed state is observable. full-field-matrix has all states but none of the three combinations.

slices.behavior: Three-way record merge, field level: non-overlapping fields union, same-field conflicts resolved last-writer-wins on `updated` and commutatively, temporal date/time pairs resolved as one value, tags unioned, body prefix-append, state progression, and the schema-version refusals on all three sides
oracle_gaps: The delegation object and the structural (add/delete/order) rules are the other two merge slices'. This slice covers scalar fields, the two temporal pairs, tags, body and state only.

The merge's version rule is NOT the store's: `allow_older` is true for the base and false for both sides, so a base at an older version still merges while a side at any version other than Format::VERSION refuses. A port that reuses `Store#unsupported_schema?` here would refuse merges git can currently resolve. This asymmetry has no counterpart anywhere else in the codebase and is the single most likely misport in the slice.

`updated` and `line` are excluded from the merge (EXCLUDED_FIELDS) but `updated` is also the tiebreaker — the field the merge reads and never writes. Nothing in the suite asserts what the merged record's own `updated` value ends up as, because the driver leaves it to the next write. Characterization must pin it before translating.

Merge decisions are logged as events and the log text is written to `.tasks-merge.log` by the driver, so `format_event`'s wording is observable to users. No test asserts the exact wording of more than a few events; merge-driver-git claims the log-shape test and this slice must capture the event vocabulary it produces.

unclaimed_after.reason: Deferred on principle, and this is the recommendation I would most like reviewed. Each of these asserts over the entire CliCommands::ALL table — 50 commands including `recur` and `lead` (campaign 5), `undo` and `redo` (campaign 6), `-p` (campaign 10). No slice can claim them honestly until those campaigns land, and seeding a 'CLI parity' slice now would put an issue in `td ready` that no agent can finish, with depends_on edges that cannot be written because the slices they would point at do not exist. td-940935 already removed two of these from cli-read-json-envelopes for exactly this reason; re-adding them under a different slice id would undo that finding. What they need is one final parity slice, seeded when campaigns 5, 6 and 8 exist, whose whole job is 'every command in the registry, one JSON document, one gate rule'. Recommend recording that as a td issue now so the obligation is not carried only by this file.

Out of scope for campaigns 2-7 by construction: manifest.md states that lib/tasks/api/ is the one part of the tree no campaign 2-4 slice ports, and it is still the only part of lib/tasks/ outside every slice's drift closure — which means it is also the only Ruby whose change no `drift` run would report. That is worth fixing when campaign 9 is seeded; until then it is a stated carve-out rather than a discovery. Note that task-view-projection's oracle_gaps already leans on api/representation.rb's key set as a contrast case, so the two projections are entangled and campaign 9 should be read against that slice.

Playbook item 10. Also the part of the tree whose port is least obviously required: `tasks -p` is the one command that opts out of --json with a stated reason, and an agent harness is exactly the kind of capability a port may decide to leave in Ruby or drop. Recommend a scope decision from Marcus before slicing, in the same shape as the schema-v1/org-mode decision — a slice seeded and then marked not_applicable is more expensive than a decision taken first.

Playbook item 12 and the largest single block of unclaimed tests in the repo by a wide margin. Deferred without hesitation: it is a presentation layer over capabilities the earlier campaigns own, the playbook puts it last, and slicing it before the domain is ported would produce records nobody can start.

unclaimed_after.reason: These prove behavior slices already own, through the store's older line-based verbs rather than through the changeset API. Seeding slices for them would double-claim behavior, which the brief forbids and which would inflate the denominator without adding coverage. They are listed because several of them are the ONLY oracle for a branch an existing slice's fixtures_todo says it cannot reach — the deferred-clear direction especially. WIRING may add any of them to the named slice's ruby_tests; `reach` will accept them because the verbs resolve to the owning slice itself.

Called out separately because it is the one genuinely unported READ behavior this survey found outside the temporal work. `headline` renders state, priority, title and tags into one string, it is a key in every mutation JSON row (`report_touched`'s item_json) and in `tasks show`, and no slice's behavior statement mentions it. It is three tests and belongs in task-view-projection rather than in a slice of its own.

operation_context.rb carries operation_id/source/actor through the Application facade and its own comment says commands do not interpret it yet — there is no observable behavior to port, and it should be seeded with campaign 9's audit seam or marked not_applicable, not sliced now. test/test_manifest_issues.rb and test/test_porting_* test the porting harness itself, which is not part of the product being ported. The two require-boundary tests assert an architectural invariant of the Ruby tree (what may require what) that has no meaning in Go.

verb_owners_additions.note: porting/manifest-issues' VERB_OWNERS maps nine of these verbs to nil today. Until it is updated, `reach` will report every ruby_test in the new slices as reaching an '(unseeded)' verb and will exit non-zero on the unexplained ones. porting/manifest-issues is GATE's path, not SLICING's, so this is a request, not a change.
